comments.author: doctoboggan
comments.textRawHtml:
How do they plan on stopping me from using Claude code with the Claude in chrome plugin, or some other computer use agent?

At this point it feels like I have an adversarial relationship with many merchants I use online. I wish the simple “you have a product, I have money” relationship was possible. I don’t want to take part in your giant human behavior optimization problem. You have a product and I have money why does it have to be more complicated than that?

Realistically though I know that’s not happening. I will continue to access online merchants in the way I prefer and will do my best to avoid detection or blocking. At least so far Claude is happy to play along but I suspect I will need to seek out an obliterated agent in the not to distant future. (Once the corporate capture of the frontier cloud AI models is complete.)

children.author: rafabulsing
children.textRawHtml: The point isn't that both are using something that might be labeled AI. The point is that the relationship is 100% adversarial at this point, and so you shouldn't feel too bad for asking for a refund when your AI makes a mistake. The company certainly doesn't feel bad, and in fact puts huge amounts of effort into extracting the maximum value not just in general but from you specifically, so maybe just go ahead and do the same to them.

children.author: akudha
children.textRawHtml:
Over the years, I have shopped quite a bit (for me anyway) at Amazon. Up until last year, I never returned a single product (even when the product wasn't upto what the description promised). I haven't (yet) left a single bad review.

Since last year, I have returned a couple of items. I also have drastically reduced shopping at Amazon. I have a lot of patience compared to some people, who abuse Amazon's return policy. That said, there is a limit to anyone's patience.

What I am trying to say is - "maybe go to different ones" might not always be possible. If you are in a hurry to get somewhere (maybe a family member is in the hospital) and a United flight is the only one available, what then? Also, other airlines are not super great either.

Maybe for some household item I can shop around at leisure, but "maybe go to different ones" is not possible all the time. Plus, shopping is tiring and irritating as it is, not everyone wants to do PhD level research for every item they buy

children.author: hbarka
children.textRawHtml:
Economy-class airline seats have generally become smaller, particularly in terms of legroom. Seat width has also declined. Why? Obviously higher capacity, greater revenue, segmentation to force upgrades.  
The situation is even more noticeable because the average American passenger has grown larger. United also has hub dominance in concentrated areas, which leaves one with practically no choice. It is a race to the bottom.

children.author: rafabulsing
children.textRawHtml:
I'm not advocating for a race to the bottom. I think we're at the bottom already, and sadly nothing we can do personally is going to change that.

I don't want people to go out of their way to hurt the companies, purposefully buying tickets they don't want and then refunding them or something. I'm just saying that on the occasion that a mistake happens, you shouldn't feel bad about using whatever legal/procedural recourse available so that you don't have to just eat the cost.

I would go for alternative airlines if there were any. Alas.

children.author: rafabulsing
children.textRawHtml:
What do you mean by "so strongly disagree with"?

I've plainly stated that I don't think they are bad to the point you should go out of your way just to attack them.

I also didn't say they are evil, destroying the world or anything like that. If that's what I thought, then yeah, stopping doing business with them altogether might be the best course of action.

But I simply said that you shouldn't feel bad about making use of recourses made available to you by either the law or the company itself. Which I don't think it's at all incongruent with continuing to use these companies' services.

children.author: mancerayder
children.textRawHtml:
What different ones? Do you live in the US? There are 30ish percent less airlines than there were in 2009 due to consolidations. There are hubs where airlines monopolize entire airports and drive costs up.

Have you ever been to Europe, if you are living in the US? I'd like you to compare costs of flying regionally there compared to here.

Airlines are just another example of oligarchic control - it's incredible that people are expressing sympathy here as if the consumer and the airlines are on equal footing. I hope you enjoy your customized dynamic pricing based on personal information they've collected about you.

Fuck you, airlines.
